text:
alyssa: quick summary from the regional kernel sweep we ran last night (flashv2 / flashv3 / triton vendor). posting raw p50/p95 and a short note on fallback behavior we should consider. TL;DR: flashv3-q8 on H100 gives best median but we see p95 spikes in eu-west-1 for long contexts (>=1024). wondering if we should enable auto-fallback to triton for p95-sensitive routes.

sam: raw numbers from the job (tokens/sec and latency ms). these are averaged over ~1h windows: 
```
us-west-2 (H100): flashv3-q8 -> p50 18ms, p95 95ms, throughput 16k tok/s
                   triton-q8  -> p50 22ms, p95 120ms, throughput 14k tok/s
eu-west-1 (H100): flashv3-q8 -> p50 20ms, p95 240ms, throughput 14k tok/s
                   triton-q8  -> p50 24ms, p95 130ms, throughput 13k tok/s
a1 (A100-ish):    flashv3-q8 -> p50 28ms, p95 150ms, throughput 10k tok/s
                   triton-q8  -> p50 30ms, p95 160ms, throughput 9.5k tok/s
```
notes: q8 quantized models. runs used 1024 context, batch sizes varied to target 95th lat performance.

leo: interesting that eu-west p95 is so bad with flashv3. could be noisy neighbor/PCIe gen differences or region thermal throttling. did we check kernel selection logs for fallback attempts?

alyssa: yes, checked logs. flashv3 kernel stays active; no automatic fallback. we only have hysteresis for region-level kernel rollouts, not per-request p95 triggers. logs show occasional CUDA mem spikes and kernel retries around the p95 windows.

jen: would it be safe to implement a policy like: if p95 > 2x baseline or latency slope > threshold for 5m, route new requests to triton for that model variant in that region for N minutes? fallback should be per-model+quantization (q8) and per-region. also add a cooldown. :thinking_face:

sam: sounds reasonable. suggested rule: 
 - trigger if p95 / p50 > 6 OR p95 increased > 80ms compared to last 30m baseline
 - fallback target: triton-q8 on same instance type if available, else fallback to lower-quant (q4) only for non-SLO routes
 - cooldown 10 minutes, require 3 consecutive windows to re-promote flashv3

leo: add metric for kernel internal retries and kernel-launch failures as part of the trigger. if kernel retries > 0.5% we flip immediately. those retries indicate instability in the kernel path.

infra-bot: benchmark job 1845078888 completed. artifacts uploaded: s3://redwood-bench/1845078888/ (latency CSVs, perf flamegraphs, kernel-logs.tar.gz) :white_check_mark:

alyssa: good. other caveats: flashv3 shows better throughput at high concurrency due to better kernel fusion and attention tiling, so fallback will cost some throughput. for Dedicated customers with throughput commitments we may need a different policy (prefer throughput over p95).

jen: agree. propose two policy flavors: 
 - latency-first (default for hosted public API chat endpoints): prioritize p95, fallback quickly to triton if triggered.
 - throughput-first (for dedicated): only fallback if kernel failures/retries exceed threshold or if sustained p95 catastrophes for >30m.

sam: also saw vendor lib (cuDNN/cuBLAS fused attention) on H100 had lower variance in eu-west but slightly worse median than flashv3. maybe another candidate for fallback chain: flashv3 -> vendor -> triton.

leo: ordering OK: flashv3 (best median) -> vendor (stable median/p95) -> triton (fallback compatibility). we should store per-region decision matrix in the model profile so rollouts can be automatic.

alyssa: next steps: 1) implement trigger + cooldown in routing service (PR queued), 2) add kernel retry metric to alerts, 3) run a week-long canary in eu-west with fallback enabled for low-SLA routes. I'll open a PR for the routing changes and tag you all.

jen: thanks — please include the exact trigger thresholds in the PR description so ops can tune. also add an opt-out flag for Dedicated customers.

sam: adding one more: for quantization experiments, note that flashv3-q4 had lower p95 variance in eu-west but reduced quality on evals by ~1.8% exact-match on our eval set. so fallback to lower-quant should be limited to non-critical paths.

alyssa: noted. will add eval regression thresholds to the rollout policy (e.g., max 1% quality drop without human review).

leo: cool. thanks all. :rocket:
